subject: Deployment mode & migration follow-up \u0014 Aurora Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Grey <tom.grey@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + next steps on deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of Aurora's requirements (from our notes):
- Production inference for patient-facing summarization and triage workflows (low-latency critical paths).
- Strong data isolation and HIPAA controls — KMS integration required.
- Expected steady throughput: ~120 qps peak across region, with occasional bursts to 300 qps.
- Primary migration from OpenAI API for dev workloads and a legacy self-hosted GPU cluster for on-prem models.

Deployment modes we discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest to production, lowest engineering lift, but would require a contract for PHI processing and careful routing to dedicated pools for compliance.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools (predictable throughput) with network-level isolation and optional private networking; good fit if you want predictable SLOs without managing infra.
3) Private VPC / On-prem — full control, integrates with your on-prem cluster or private VPC; best for air-gapped/regulatory needs but longer lead time.

What we recommend based on your constraints: Primary move to Dedicated capacity for production inference (meets throughput + latency + KMS needs), with a plan to evaluate Private VPC for limited workloads that must remain on-prem. Hosted API could be used for non-PHI dev workloads to accelerate rollout.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll share a Dedicated capacity pricing packet and a migration checklist (attached).
- Rishi / Dev — can you confirm typical instance types and an initial sizing estimate based on 120 qps baseline?
- Tom — can you confirm who on your infra/security team I should loop in (legal already copied)?
- Schedule a technical migration workshop next week to map current self-hosted cluster to Redwood Dedicated nodes (30–45 min).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf, aurora-migration-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Tom Grey <tom.grey@aurorahealth.com>

Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + next steps on deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That matches our internal notes. A few clarifications: 

- Confirmed: HIPAA scope will cover the production inference paths. We need KMS/HSM support and audit logs for >90 days.
- Migration sources: primary is OpenAI API (production traffic today ~40 qps), secondary is a legacy GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100 nodes) used for model training and some inference. The cluster is behind our private network and we’re exploring hybrid approaches.
- Preference: dedicated capacity for the initial cutover. We like predictable throughput and simpler rollback. Private VPC makes sense for a later wave for fully regulated datasets.

Please loop in your Solutions/Engineering folks for the tech workshop. I’ll bring our infra lead (Sasha Ivanov) and legal will review the SOC2 snapshot.

Can we do Thu 6/3 at 10:00 PT for the migration workshop?

Thanks,
Tom
Director of Product — Aurora Health
Tom.Grey@aurorahealth.com
(617) 555-2400

Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up + next steps on deployment mode (migration workshop request)

Rishi / Dev — forwarding Aurora's confirmation. They want Dedicated capacity initially and asked for a migration workshop on Thu 6/3 at 10:00 PT. Key asks from Aurora: KMS/HSM support, audit logs retention 90+ days, and proof points on cold-start latency for 4k token summaries.

Can you please: 
- Share a slide or short doc with typical Dedicated sizing for ~120 qps baseline and burst to 300 qps, including expected token throughput and preferred instance types.
- Prepare a short checklist for migrating from OpenAI APIs and a mapping document for self-hosted cluster -> Redwood Dedicated (what model formats we support, kv cache behavior, quantization notes).
- Bring someone who can speak to KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention (and whether we can provide an export snapshot for their legal team).

I attached the pricing & migration checklist I sent to them. If anything blocks the 6/3 time, propose alternatives.

Thanks — I’ll run the meeting and handle product questions.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf, aurora-migration-checklist.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Grey <tom.grey@aurorahealth.com>, Legal <legal@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick follow-up + next steps on deployment mode (migration workshop request)

Thanks Marissa — I’ll own the migration workshop content. Quick notes before the call:

- Initial sizing: for 120 qps baseline (assuming ~30 tokens per request average, 4k token max for summaries), plan for a pool with 8 x A100-class GPUs (reserved) with autoscale headroom to add 4 more for bursts; we’ll provide a more exact projection with token/sec estimates.
- Migration checklist highlights: model format compatibility (PT/ONNX/ GGUF conversion notes), KV cache warm-up strategies, prefix caching for common prompts, and estimation of cost delta vs OpenAI per token.
- KMS/HSM: we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private modes; we can deliver an audit-log export (S3 snapshot) and are willing to provide SOC2 snapshot (attached).

I’ll drop a short sizing doc and the migration mapping before EOD Tuesday so you can share with Aurora ahead of Thu.

	64Dev

dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
